maria: Heads-up — noticed a regression in host pre-parse since the kernel-selector flip this morning. p99 tail for small requests jumped ~18% on the canary cluster. attaching quick notes below.
aj: saw the alert. rough numbers?
maria: baseline p99 ~12ms, now 14.3–15ms for the same traffic mix (small text gen, <200 tokens). throughput steady.
ryan: I ran a flame on the canary. hot path looks like: pretoken::normalize -> memmove -> net::readv -> kvcache::lookup. Memmove is surprisingly high.
sam: do we have diffs for the kernel selection? which variant was chosen that might affect host-side layout?
ryan: the selector rolled back to the newer kernel bin that changed block alignment (64->128) for the tokenize buffer allocation. suspecting extra padding -> extra memcpy.
maria: timeline: selector change at 09:58, canary traffic routed at 10:01, alert fired 10:12. infra-bot deployed an emergency rollback 10:30. still seeing traces from the period.
aj: can you paste perf top snippet?
ryan: ```
Samples: 4K of event 'cpu-cycles'
   40.2% pretoken::normalize
   21.7% host::memmove
   11.5% net::readv
    9.8% kvcache::lookup
    5.6% grpc::slice_merge
    3.4% other
```
maria: interesting that grpc slice_merge shows up — might be extra chunk copies during stream framing.
sam: reproduction steps I ran: replay small-req load with --seq-len 128 and --concurrency 50. Add benchmark command: `./bench/run --profile=flame --reqs=10k --seq=128 --concurrency=50`. Saw same memmove spike.
aj: quick mitigation idea: re-enable the old kernel bin for host allocations (the one with 64 alignment) until we can retune batching heuristics.
ryan: agree. also want to test reducing the default batch timeout by 1ms to see if it reduces grpc slice_merge pressure (fewer partial frames).
maria: action items: 1) infra-bot rollback to old kernel bin on canary (done 10:30) 2) aj to run A/B with batch timeout -1ms vs baseline 3) ryan to add microbench for allocator alignment and memmove counts 4) sam to produce per-route KV hit/miss breakdown during window.
aj: I'll kick off the A/B. starting tests now.
sam: KV numbers while spike present: route /v1/generate: hit=82%, miss=18% (slightly worse than baseline 85/15). small difference but could amplify mem pressure.
ryan: note: memmove is mostly in the pretoken buffer compact step — we do a left-shift to coalesce fragments after token boundary detection. We can try an in-place compact that avoids an extra memmove when no fragmentation present. I'll prototype.
maria: keep changes small and scoped; we want to avoid introducing more regressions. Post observations in this thread.
infra-bot: Canary roll back to kernel-bin v2.14 completed at 10:30:45. Health checks green.
aj: early A/B results: batch timeout -1ms reduces p95 by ~2%, p99 unchanged yet. continuing. :thinking_face: 
ryan: pushed a microbenchmark PR for in-place compact (w/ unit tests). perf diff locally: memmove time down 55% on microbench, end-to-end p99 down 0.8ms in replay. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1234
sam: I'll correlate KV pressure with GC/alloc spikes — sending heap profiles. small requests see a small uptick in short-lived allocations when alignment changed.
maria: summary for the pager: root cause: kernel selector chose allocation bin with different alignment/padding which increased host-side memcpy and grpc slice merges during streaming. mitigations: rollback selector (done), batch timeout experiment, and in-place compact PR. Follow-ups: validate on canary for 24h and run full e2e regression checks.
aj: LGTM. thanks all. :thumbsup:
